subject: creative_writing

resources.title: Introduction to Fiction
resources.notes: Communications-intensive fiction course requiring polished writing and revision; useful for narrative craft and revision evidence.

resources.title: Reading Poetry
resources.notes: Formal tools include meter, sound, syntax, word choice, metaphor, rhythm, analytic writing and revision.

resources.title: Playwriting I
resources.notes: Craft-focused theater writing with scene structure, action, events, voice, dialogue, weekly exercises and a sustained project.

resources.title: Writing and Reading the Essay
resources.notes: Writing-centered study of the literary essay and nonfiction prose with assignment examples.

resources.title: Forms of Western Narrative
resources.notes: Studies changing narrative forms and how historical, cultural and technological contexts shape storytelling.

resources.title: Project Gutenberg Literature Corpus
resources.notes: Primary-text corpus including dramatic works for reading, comparison and craft research; this is source material rather than a playwriting curriculum, and individual editions remain provenance-tracked.

resources.title: Computational Creativity and Writing Research
resources.notes: Research layer only; individual papers require relevance, quality and license review before ingestion.

resources.title: Start Writing Fiction
resources.notes: Provider identifies this as Level 1 introductory study covering character, setting and genre. Worldbuilding mapping is limited to its explicit instruction on creating settings and interactions between character and place.

resources.title: Writing What You Know
resources.notes: Level 1 introductory course using memory, observation, sensory detail and personal history, with an explicit section on building a believable world.

resources.title: Screenplay Format for TV Shows
resources.notes: Practical introductory reference for television screenplay layout and formatting. It does not by itself provide a complete screenwriting curriculum.

resources.title: Shavelson-Webb Library and Writers Guild Foundation Archive
resources.notes: Research library with more than 50,000 produced film and television scripts plus drafts, treatments, outlines, pitches and show bibles. Materials are primarily on-site and cannot be copied, emailed, borrowed or redistributed; catalog coverage must not be interpreted as digitally ingestible content.

known_gaps: Screenwriting foundation and research references are present, but a balanced open digital curriculum remains thinner than fiction and playwriting coverage.
Graduate-level workshop and publishing-practice coverage needs stronger open, directly auditable curricula rather than being inferred from undergraduate courses.
Research repositories do not establish expert creative-writing readiness without portfolio work, iterative critique, revision evidence and assessment.
The Writers Guild Foundation archive is primarily an in-person research resource and must not be counted as runtime-ingestible script content.
